Subject: Novex + Redwood: Integration kickoff and SDK questions

Hi Logan —

Thanks for the intro earlier. Novex is excited to get started integrating Redwood for our in-app assistant. Before we lock a kickoff time, a few quick things from our side so we can prepare the right engineers: 

- Which SDKs do you recommend for a server-side integration that will call the Redwood hosted API (Node + Go)?
- Do you have a short checklist for pre-kickoff tasks (API keys, network whitelists, compliance forms)?
- We'll likely need guidance on endpoint migration (we currently run a legacy model endpoint on our gateway) and on safe retry/backoff defaults — our gateway tends to enforce strict timeouts (2s per upstream request).

Can you send an agenda and any sample code we can pre-load for the call? Also cc'ing our API team (api-team@novex.com) so they have context.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Product Integrations
Novex Systems

Subject: Re: Novex + Redwood: Integration kickoff and SDK questions

Hi Elena —

Great to hear — welcome aboard. Attached a short integration checklist (novex-integration-checklist.xlsx) and a zipped sample repo (redwood-sample-code-v1.zip) with Node and Go examples that follow our recommended patterns. High-level answers: 

- SDK recommendations: Server-side Node SDK (node-redwood) works well for async batching; Go SDK (go-redwood) is lean for low-latency single requests. Both support streaming responses.
- Pre-kickoff checklist: API key + role scoped key, egress CIDR whitelist (we'll provide IPs), HubSpot mutual action plan + security questionnaire if needed.
- Endpoint migration: we suggest a phased cutover (shadow -> canary -> cut) with traffic split and automatic fallback to hosted stable model.
- Retries/timeouts: default client timeout = 10s, connection retry with exponential backoff (base 200ms, max 2s, 3 attempts) — we can adapt to your gateway 2s limit by shifting retries to the SDK’s client-side circuit breaker rather than refiring identical upstream requests.

Proposed kickoff agenda (30–45m):
1) Introductions + goals (5m)
2) Run through checklist & access (5m)
3) Sample code walkthrough (10m)
4) Endpoint migration plan & rollback criteria (10m)
5) Next steps & owners (5m)

I'll schedule a 45-minute slot once you confirm availability. Monica (cc'd) will lead the implementation handoff.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Strategic Integrations, Redwood Inference

Attachments: novex-integration-checklist.xlsx, redwood-sample-code-v1.zip

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@novex.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jul 2028 08:00:00 -0700
Subject: Novex integration: SDK onboarding & endpoint migration plan (detailed)

Elena / Novex API team —

Thanks for the availability — we'll take the 7/18 08:00 PT slot. Below is a concise technical playbook we will walk through on the kickoff. I'll attach the markdown runbook (runbook-sdk-endpoint-migration.md) to the meeting invite.

1) Short architecture recommendation (pattern we will demo)
- Edge gateway (your infra) -> Streaming aggregation proxy (lightweight service in your VPC) -> Redwood server-side SDK (long-lived backend connection).
- Reason: your 2s request timeout remains satisfied at the edge; streaming proxy accepts short client requests and provides immediate acknowledgement and streaming to UI while the backend handles model tokenization and retries.

2) Idempotency + retries
- Pattern: SDK attaches Idempotency-Key header for any non-idempotent request (UUID v4). For streaming or user-initiated prompts, generate a per-session request-id + message-sequence. Example header: Idempotency-Key: novex-<sessionId>-<messageSeq>-<unixTs>.
- Retry policy (recommended):
  - On network/5xx: exponential backoff with jitter (base 150ms, multiplier 2, max interval 1600ms), 3 attempts.
  - If your gateway dedupes based on body + idempotency key, the second attempt will be ignored safely.

3) Timeouts
- Client-facing timeout at edge: 2s to the proxy (ACK + stream negotiation).
- Proxy -> Redwood SDK timeout: 12s (to allow model token generation spikes).
- Circuit breaker: open after 5 consecutive 5xx / timeouts for 60s, half-open probe after 30s.

4) Rate limiting & batching guidance
- Your peak 600 rps: favor request batching where possible. Use micro-batches for short prompts (group by session/window up to 8 concurrent prompts or 1–2 second window).
- Enable prefix/KV caching on the SDK for repeated system prompts to reduce token usage. We'll suggest specific cache TTLs during the call based on your prompt patterns.

5) Endpoint migration (shadow -> canary -> cutover)
- Shadow (2 days): send 10% of traffic to Redwood in shadow mode (no user-facing responses). Monitor latencies and token cost.
- Canary (3 days): route 5–10% real traffic and enable fast rollback. Validate quality via a short eval set.
- Cutover: increase to steady-state (agreed %) with capacity ramp. Rollback plan: DNS/traffic swap + immediate route to legacy endpoint; have canary metrics watch (error rate >1.5x or 99th pctl latency breach).

6) Sample code snippet (Node pseudo-example for idempotent call)
const { RedwoodClient } = require('node-redwood');
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });

async function sendPrompt(sessionId, seq, prompt) {
  const idempotencyKey = `novex-${sessionId}-${seq}-${Date.now()}`;
  try {
    const res = await client.generate({
      model: 'redwood-3b',
      prompt,
      headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': idempotencyKey },
      timeout: 12000 // ms for proxy->sdk
    });
    return res;
  } catch (err) {
    // handle retry with backoff here (see recommended policy)
    throw err;
  }
}

7) Observability & SLOs
- We'll add request-level tracing (trace-id header) that correlates with Redwood Console logs. Grace will add the runbook section that lists the tracing headers to include.

Next steps (owners):
- Monica: Provision sandbox keys + create the HubSpot MAP (today).
- Vivek: Draft SDK proxy example + unit tests (due: 2028-07-20).
- Grace: Publish runbook to Drive + attach to meeting invite (done).
- Novex: Confirm OCI/CIDR whitelist and share a contact for the on-call engineer.

We'll walk through the sample code and the migration windows on the kickoff. Looking forward to it.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Strategic Integrations, Redwood Inference
